easy.explanation: Hezekiah was the son of Ahaz, king of Judah.

answers: He served the king of Assyria
easy.explanation: The KJV says that Hezekiah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD.
easy.q: How is Hezekiah described in the sight of the LORD?

easy.explanation: Hezekiah broke the brazen serpent because the children of Israel burned incense to it.
easy.q: What did Hezekiah do to the brazen serpent?

answers: Because the people burned incense to it
Because it was made of metal
medium.explanation: The people had begun treating the serpent as an object of worship.
medium.q: Why did Hezekiah break the brazen serpent?

answers: He remained faithful to the LORD
He made a covenant with the Philistines
medium.explanation: To cleave to the LORD means to remain closely devoted and faithful to him.
medium.q: What does the statement that Hezekiah “clave to the LORD” show?

answers: He removed idolatry and rebelled against Assyria
He served Assyria and restored the high places
medium.explanation: Hezekiah removed idolatrous practices, rebelled against Assyria, and defeated the Philistines.
medium.q: How did Hezekiah combine religious reform with political action?

answers: His trust and devotion are presented alongside his prosperity
His trust caused him to serve Assyria
The passage gives no connection between them
challenge.explanation: Hezekiah trusted and clave to the LORD, and the LORD was with him so that he prospered.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between trusting the LORD and Hezekiah's success?

answers: He removed the high places only
He broke the brazen serpent that Moses had made
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically says that Moses had made the brazen serpent, yet the people burned incense to it.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Hezekiah opposed a practice connected even with Moses?

answers: He was the first king of Judah
He was unusually devoted to the LORD
challenge.explanation: The statement highlights Hezekiah's exceptional faithfulness among Judah's kings.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the statement that there was none like Hezekiah among the kings of Judah?

paragraphs.title: The Fall of Samaria and the Exile of Israel

easy.explanation: Shalmaneser king of Assyria came against Samaria and besieged it.
Samaria was taken at the end of three years.
easy.q: About how long did the siege of Samaria last?

easy.explanation: The king of Assyria carried Israel away unto Assyria.
easy.q: Where were the Israelites carried away?

medium.explanation: At the end of three years, Samaria was captured.
medium.q: What was the result of the siege of Samaria?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the removal of Israel from its land into Assyrian territory.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “carry away” mean?

answers: Because Israel disobeyed the LORD and transgressed his covenant
Because of a lack of food alone
Because Israel wanted to move to Assyria
medium.explanation: The passage says they obeyed not the voice of the LORD and transgressed his covenant.
medium.q: How does the passage explain Israel's exile?

answers: The sins are presented as the background and reason for the exile
The sins are presented as the reason for Hezekiah's accession
challenge.explanation: The historical capture is followed by a theological explanation centered on Israel's disobedience.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the account of Samaria's capture and the explanation of Israel's sins?

answers: The mention of Halah, Habor, Gozan, and the cities of the Medes
challenge.explanation: Several regions and cities are listed as places where the exiles were settled.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes that the exile involved several different destinations?

answers: First came the siege, then the capture, and finally the exile
First came the exile and then the siege
Judah was exiled before Samaria was captured
challenge.explanation: The sequence is siege, capture of Samaria, and deportation of Israel.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the order of events in the passage?

paragraphs.title: Sennacherib's Campaign and Hezekiah's Temporary Submission

answers: Only the cities of the Philistines
easy.explanation: Sennacherib came against all the fenced cities of Judah and took them.
easy.q: Against which cities did Sennacherib come?

easy.explanation: Hezekiah said, “I have offended; return from me.”
easy.q: What did Hezekiah ask Sennacherib to do?

answers: Three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold
easy.explanation: The king of Assyria appointed Hezekiah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
easy.q: What payment was imposed on Hezekiah?

answers: Only money from the people's homes
Silver from the LORD's house and the king's treasures
medium.explanation: Hezekiah gave silver found in the house of the LORD and in the treasures of the king's house.
medium.q: What sources of wealth did Hezekiah give to the king of Assyria?

answers: A unit of weight or value
The name of an Assyrian officer
medium.explanation: A talent was a large unit of weight used here for silver and gold.
medium.q: In the KJV passage, what is a “talent”?

answers: To give the gold to the king of Assyria
medium.explanation: He removed the gold and gave it to the king of Assyria as part of the required payment.
medium.q: Why did Hezekiah cut the gold from the doors of the temple?

answers: The passage also describes temporary submission under pressure
Hezekiah completely stopped believing in the LORD
challenge.explanation: After Assyria captured Judah's cities, Hezekiah temporarily submitted and paid tribute.
challenge.q: What does the movement from Hezekiah's trust in the LORD to his payment to Assyria show?

answers: He gave only his personal property
He gave from both the temple treasury and the royal treasury
challenge.explanation: The payment drew upon both the house of the LORD and the king's treasures.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the size of the price Hezekiah paid?

answers: Judah was under severe Assyrian pressure
challenge.explanation: The conquest and the imposed payment reveal Assyria's strong position over Judah.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Sennacherib setting the payment after conquering the cities?

paragraphs.title: The Assyrian Envoys Arrive at Jerusalem

easy.explanation: The king of Assyria sent these officials to Jerusalem.
easy.q: Who sent Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rab-shakeh?

easy.explanation: They came with a great host against Jerusalem.
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah came out to meet them.
easy.q: Who went out to meet the officials on Hezekiah's behalf?

answers: By the conduit of the upper pool
In the king of Assyria's palace
medium.explanation: They stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field.
medium.q: Where did the Assyrian officials stand?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a large military force.
medium.q: What does the phrase “a great host” mean?

answers: A formal meeting took place between the two sides
medium.explanation: The representatives' appearance indicates an official diplomatic meeting.
medium.q: What can be understood from Hezekiah's representatives going out to meet the envoys?

answers: It emphasizes the military threat behind their mission
It proves they came for a celebration
It shows they had no connection with the king of Assyria
challenge.explanation: The accompanying army made the delegation an immediate military threat, not merely a diplomatic visit.
challenge.q: Why is it important that the envoys came with a great host rather than alone?

answers: The meeting occurred near Jerusalem's waterworks and outside the royal center
challenge.explanation: The passage carefully locates the meeting by the upper pool and the fuller's field.
challenge.q: What does the precise description of the meeting place emphasize?

answers: A great Assyrian host facing Judean representatives
challenge.explanation: A large Assyrian force is contrasted with the small delegation sent by Hezekiah.
challenge.q: What contrast is prominent in this scene?

easy.explanation: Rab-shakeh asked, “What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?”
He called Egypt a bruised reed that would pierce the hand of anyone leaning on it.

answers: That the LORD had commanded him to come
That Egypt had commanded him to come
easy.explanation: Rab-shakeh claimed that the LORD had said, “Go up against this land, and destroy it.”
easy.q: What did Rab-shakeh claim about Assyria's advance against the land?

answers: To portray Egypt as an unreliable support
To offer an alliance with Egypt
medium.explanation: The image suggests that Egypt could not safely support or protect Judah.
medium.q: Why did Rab-shakeh compare Egypt to a bruised reed?

medium.explanation: He dismissed Hezekiah's claims of counsel and strength as empty or ineffective speech.
medium.q: What does Rab-shakeh mean by “vain words”?

answers: He claimed that removing the high places and altars had offended the LORD
He claimed that Hezekiah had built many altars
He praised Hezekiah for removing idols
medium.explanation: Rab-shakeh falsely presented Hezekiah's religious reforms as an offense against the LORD.
medium.q: How did Rab-shakeh use Hezekiah's reform against him?

answers: He claimed the LORD sent Assyria to destroy, while also questioning the LORD's power to save
He claimed that Assyria did not exist
He admitted that Judah had defeated Assyria
challenge.explanation: Rab-shakeh invoked the LORD to justify Assyria while denying that the LORD could deliver Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What is the central contradiction in Rab-shakeh's claims about the LORD?

answers: He ridiculed Egypt and Judah's military strength and portrayed the reform as opposition to the LORD
He offered to strengthen Judah's army
challenge.explanation: His speech attacked both Judah's proposed military support and its religious confidence.
challenge.q: How did Rab-shakeh attack Hezekiah both militarily and religiously?

answers: He was trying to undermine every basis of Judah's confidence
He wanted Judah to worship Egypt
challenge.explanation: He attacked both Judah's hope for political aid and its trust in the LORD.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Rab-shakeh mentioning both Egypt and the LORD?

paragraphs.title: The Rabshakeh's Propaganda Speech and the Response

easy.explanation: They asked him to speak in the Syrian language rather than in the Jews' language.
easy.q: In what language did Hezekiah's representatives ask Rab-shakeh to speak?

answers: The people sitting on the wall
easy.explanation: Rab-shakeh stood and cried with a loud voice to the people on the wall.
easy.q: To whom did Rab-shakeh eventually speak?

easy.explanation: The people held their peace and answered him not a word.
easy.q: How did the people respond to Rab-shakeh?

answers: They understood Syrian and did not want the people on the wall to understand
Syrian was only the enemy's language
medium.explanation: They asked him not to speak in the Jews' language in the ears of the people on the wall.
medium.q: Why did the representatives ask Rab-shakeh to speak in the Syrian language?

answers: Food and drink in their own land until he took them to a good land
medium.explanation: He promised that they could eat and drink before being taken to a land like their own, described as fruitful and good.
medium.q: What did the king of Assyria offer the people if they came out to him?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that the people kept silent and did not answer Rab-shakeh.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “held their peace” mean?

answers: He addressed the people directly, promised them better conditions, and attacked their faith
He refused to speak to the people
He spoke only with the king of Assyria
challenge.explanation: Rab-shakeh sought to influence the people through fear, promises, and attacks on their confidence in the LORD.
challenge.q: How did Rab-shakeh act as a propagandist and not merely as a military envoy?

answers: Assyria presented surrender as a path to prosperity while seeking to control the people
Assyria promised war while offering peace
Assyria promised to leave the people in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The offer sounded attractive, but it required the people to leave Jerusalem and come under Assyrian rule.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Assyria's promise and its real purpose?

answers: They returned with torn clothes and reported Rab-shakeh's words to Hezekiah
They answered with a speech of their own
challenge.explanation: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah returned to Hezekiah with their clothes rent and told him the words of Rab-shakeh.
challenge.q: What does the ending of the passage reveal about Hezekiah's representatives?
